Arequipa earned the nickname "White City" because of the pale volcanic stone widely used in its architecture. The historic center brings together colonial buildings, churches, monasteries and squares.

The main historic landmark is the Santa Catalina Monastery. A city tour also takes in the cathedral, La Compañía Church, San Francisco, Santo Domingo, Plaza de Armas, Casa de la Moneda and Casa Moral.

Arequipa combines well with the natural side of a journey. Agricultural terraces survive around the city, and a trip to Colca Canyon remains one of the main routes out of Arequipa.

The Argentine Islands lie off the western coast of the Antarctic Peninsula. The Penola Strait separates them from Graham Land. The group includes many small islands and rocks with sea channels running between them.

The islands were charted by members of the French Antarctic Expedition of 1903–1905 and named in honor of Argentina. They are part of Antarctic geography. On a journey south, they become part of the ice-and-island scenery en route to the Crystal Sound area.

## San Blas Islands!

The San Blas archipelago comprises 375 islands stretching along Panama's Caribbean coast, from San Blas Bay to the Colombian border.

## The Distinctive Character of the San Blas Archipelago!

Most of the islands are very small and uninhabited. You can take a tour of the San Blas archipelago and visit Indigenous villages. Fishing and diving are available in the crystal-clear waters of the Caribbean Sea. Kuna women wear traditional clothing decorated with many ornaments, including nose rings. Matriarchy still prevails here! The Kuna build their homes from palm wood, leaves and straw, yet these houses are strong enough to withstand powerful winds and downpours.

Armenia lies in Colombia's Quindío region, where city life is closely linked to coffee growing. The surrounding area is covered with plantations and farms, and introductions to the region often begin at the local El Edén Airport. This makes the city a convenient stop between a flight and journeys through the coffee valleys.

At nearby coffee estates, visitors learn how the beans are grown and processed and discover local methods of preparing the drink. From Armenia, the journey continues to Salento and the Cocora Valley, with its wax palms. The city offers a base for combining these natural and rural sights in one trip.
